sources.entry: VLC - VLC is a free and open source cross-platform multimedia player

summary.one_liner: VLC is a free, open source, cross-platform media player and multimedia engine that plays most files, discs, streams and devices, and can convert and stream media.
summary.what_it_does: VLC plays most multimedia files, discs, streams and devices, and can also convert, encode, stream and manipulate streams into many formats. Its engine, libVLC, can be embedded into third-party applications and offers playback, streaming and conversion, with bindings for C++, Python and C#. The README lists support for Windows, macOS, GNU/Linux, BSD, Android, iOS, Haiku and OS/2. The main codebase is C, with plenty of C++, Obj-C, asm and Rust. Contributions go through Merge Requests on the project's GitLab, and the README describes the source tree layout (modules/, lib/, src/, bindings/, contrib/, and others).
use_cases: play DVDs, discs and network streams
embed a media engine in an app (libVLC)
watch media on Android, iOS or desktop
how_to_run: Download a binary from the VideoLAN website (the README links to the VLC web site)
Build from source using the INSTALL file in the repository
Use the contrib/ directory to fetch and build external libraries on systems lacking them
notable: Plays almost any media format, disc, stream or device
libVLC engine can be embedded in third-party applications
Runs on many platforms including Windows, macOS, Linux, BSD, Android, iOS, Haiku and OS/2
Relicensed under GPLv2 in 2001; libVLC is LGPLv2 so it can be embedded in closed-source apps
Developed by volunteers within the VideoLAN project
caveats: Not all platforms receive the same level of care due to limited resources
On some platforms it is de facto GPLv3 because of dependency licenses
Android and iOS apps live in separate repositories
summary.license: GPLv2 (or later); libVLC is LGPLv2 (or later)
